# School Results Portal: Project Instructions (V1)

Read this file fully before every task. If a request conflicts with it, stop and ask.

## What we're building
A web portal for ONE school (nursery, primary and secondary; about 500 students; 11 classes; 3 terms a year).
- Parents log in and view their child's published results for the current term. View only.
- School staff upload results from Excel, review and approve them, and manage student records.

Version 1 only. Do not add anything that is not listed under "In scope".

## Hard constraints (the app must run on ordinary shared hosting)
- Hosting is Hostinger Business or Namecheap-style cPanel shared hosting, running one Node.js process. Therefore:
  - No Docker, Redis, queues, background workers, WebSockets, or logic that depends on cron.
  - Every request must finish well under 60 seconds (Hostinger stops requests at 120 s).
  - Database is PostgreSQL. Do NOT use MySQL-specific features. Use `pg` (or Knex) with plain SQL migrations, and `bcryptjs` (pure JS), not `bcrypt`.
  - Process Excel uploads inside the request (about 500 rows, 5 MB file limit).
- Frontend: React + Vite + TypeScript, built to static files (`dist/`). Client-side routing needs a `public/.htaccess` rewrite to `index.html`.
- Backend: Node.js + Express + TypeScript, one process, config only from environment variables (`.env.example` committed, `.env` never).
- Monorepo: `/client`, `/server`, `/docs`.

## In scope (V1)
1. Parent login: admission number + access code. One login = one child. Current term only. View only.
2. Staff login (email + password). Roles: `superadmin` (used by the administrator and the vice principal) and `teacher`. In V1 only superadmin accounts are active; teacher accounts are a feature-flagged Phase 2 feature (see "Phase 2 features").
3. Student records: import from the school's student register (Excel/CSV); add, edit, deactivate; assign to a class. Stored fields ONLY: admission number (unique), first name, last name, class, parent/guardian phone, active flag. The register also contains date of birth, parent/guardian name, parent/guardian address, religion and sex. Do NOT store, display or log those columns: ignore them on import and delete the uploaded file from disk as soon as it has been parsed. Add another field only if it appears on the printed report-card layouts, and only after I say so.
4. Access codes: generated by the system (8 characters, no look-alike characters such as 0/O/1/I/l), stored only as a hash, shown or exported once at generation. Regenerating invalidates the old code.
5. Credential export: per-class CSV (admission number, name, parent phone, code) plus a copy-ready message template, so the school sends logins itself. NO WhatsApp/SMS integration in V1.
6. Results upload: per class and term, from an Excel template, with row-level validation errors and a preview before saving. Two layouts: primary and secondary (see `/docs/layouts`).
7. Review and approval: uploaded results start as `draft`. A principal or administrator approves a batch, which makes it `published`. Parents see only published results.
8. Corrections: administrators can edit results after upload. Every edit goes to an audit log (who, when, old value, new value).
9. Results are displayed exactly as uploaded. The platform does NOT calculate totals, averages, grades or positions. They arrive as columns in the sheet.

## Out of scope (do not build, do not scaffold)
Fees or payments, attendance tracking (attendance is only a column in uploaded results), announcements, messaging, timetables, WhatsApp/SMS sending, automatic calculations, multiple children per parent login, previous-term history for parents, a mobile app, download or print buttons for parents.

## Data
- Suggested tables: `classes`, `terms`, `students`, `staff_users`, `access_codes`, `result_batches` (class, term, layout, status), `result_rows` (batch, student, data JSON), `audit_log`, `login_attempts`.
- Student import rules: match headers case-insensitively after trimming spaces (e.g. "First name", "firstname"). Class names in the register must match an existing class exactly, otherwise show a row error. Normalise Nigerian phone numbers to one format (accept 080…, 234… and +234…). The same phone number may belong to several students (siblings). Duplicate admission numbers are errors. The preview shows only the stored fields. Never write the uploaded file to a public folder, and delete it after parsing.
- Layout definitions (which sections and columns each layout shows) live in versioned JSON config files, not hard-coded in components. Subjects differ per class, so subject columns come from the uploaded sheet.
- Seed and test data must be FAKE. Never put real student names, phone numbers or results in the repo, tests, prompts or screenshots.

## Phase 2 features (build now, ship DISABLED behind feature flags)
These are built and tested now but stay switched off until the client has paid for them.
- Flags are read in ONE module (`server/src/config/features.ts`) from environment variables, all defaulting to `false`: `FEATURE_TEACHER_ACCOUNTS`, `FEATURE_STUDENT_PHOTOS`, `FEATURE_LGA_FIELD`, `FEATURE_EXPORT_REQUESTS`. List them in `.env.example` and in a "Features" table in the README.
- When a flag is off: its API routes are not mounted (or return 403 `feature_not_enabled`), its UI is hidden, and nothing else changes. Migrations create the tables and columns regardless, so enabling a flag needs no migration.
- Flags must be visible and documented. No obfuscation, no remote licence checks, no time limits, and nothing that disables a feature that is enabled.
- `FEATURE_TEACHER_ACCOUNTS`: teacher login; each teacher is assigned classes; a teacher can upload results (as draft) and view results ONLY for assigned classes. Teachers cannot approve, edit after approval, manage students or accounts, or export or print. Superadmins can add teacher and parent accounts singly or in batch (Excel/CSV with preview and row errors), reset or reassign any teacher's login, and regenerate any parent's access code. Every such action is written to the audit log.
- `FEATURE_STUDENT_PHOTOS`: a superadmin can upload one photo per student (JPG/PNG, 2 MB max, resized to 400 px, EXIF stripped), singly or in bulk from a ZIP of files named by admission number. Photos are stored outside the public web root and served only through an authenticated route to staff and to that student's own parent. Show the photo on the report-card layout when present.
- `FEATURE_LGA_FIELD`: adds a "Local government area" field to student records, the import template and the report-card layouts.
- `FEATURE_EXPORT_REQUESTS`: a teacher submits an export or print request from their dashboard; a superadmin approves or denies it; an approved export is single-use and expires. Independent of this flag, every superadmin export is written to the audit log (who, what, when).
- Tests must cover each flag both on and off, and prove a teacher can never reach another class's results.

## Security rules (non-negotiable)
- Parameterised queries only. Validate every input (zod). Escape output.
- A parent can only ever read their own child's PUBLISHED results. Write a test proving a parent cannot reach another child's results or any draft.
- Failed logins return one generic message. Rate-limit by admission number and by IP using a database table (no Redis), and lock out after repeated failures.
- Cookies: httpOnly, secure, sameSite=strict. Helmet on. CORS limited to the portal's own origin.
- Uploads: `.xlsx`/`.csv` only, 5 MB max, never executed or served back.
- Never log access codes, passwords or phone numbers.
- No secrets in the repo.

## UX rules
- Mobile first: most parents use Android phones on mobile data. Keep the bundle small, split code by route, show loading skeletons, use big touch targets and plain language.
- Admin screens are desktop-friendly tables with clear error messages.
- No download or print buttons for parents (view only).

## Working rules
- Keep changes small and tell me which files you changed.
- Do not add heavy dependencies without saying why.
- Add tests for auth, authorization and upload validation.
- Finish every task by listing what you did, what you did NOT do, and anything you are unsure about.
